headlines.title: People with Type 2 diabetes lost up to 60 pounds on Lilly’s latest weight loss drug
headlines.description: Participants who took the experimental drug retatrutide experienced the largest weight loss ever seen in a drug trial for diabetes.

headlines.title: Bruce Willis Shares Sweet Moment With His Daughter in Rare Photo
headlines.description: Tallulah Willis, daughter of Bruce Willis, shared a photo of her father online. It’s a rare glimpse into the actor’s life following his dementia diagnosis.

headlines.title: Looming changes to Medicaid work requirements spark concern with patients and caregivers
headlines.description: New Medicaid work requirements are set to take effect at the beginning of 2027 and the non-partisan Congressional Budget Office says the changes could leave 8 million more people across the country without health insurance. It has patients and caregivers concerned about their futures. NBC News' Julie Tsirkin reports.

headlines.title: End-Of-Year Doctor Appointments: How to Get One, What to Say
headlines.description: The final months of the year are approaching, so it’s time to squeeze in end-of-year doctor's appointments. Family physician Dr. Jen Caudle stops by TODAY with tips on how to get the most out of your appointments, including getting the appointment, knowing when to get a second opinion, bringing a list of symptoms to your appointment, and more.

headlines.title: How to Prepare to Fall Sports and Avoid Getting Sidelined by Injury
headlines.description: Fall sports are in full swing, so Dr. Melissa Leber, associate professor of orthopedics and emergency medicine at Mount Sinai, joins the 3rd Hour of TODAY with tips to for preventing injuries, including the benefits of cross-training, making sure shoes from prior seasons still fit properly, when to seek medical attention and more.

headlines.title: Doctors in Pennsylvania estimate at least six babies have been born with measles
headlines.description: At least six babies in Pennsylvania have been born infected with measles, with two so sick they had to be admitted to intensive care. The growing outbreak is raising alarm among doctors who are treating the potentially deadly condition. Congenital measles is a disease that’s rarely, if ever, seen in the U.S. NBC News' Erika Edwards reports.
